docs.title: Make a mod
docs.text:
CitizenSimulator separates contracts in CitizenSimulator.Abstractions from implementations in CitizenSimulator.Engine. A mod implements IMod, supplies a ModAttribute, and receives an IModContext during loading. The context provides the world, component registry, system registry, service registry, simulation clock, queued controls, and two event buses.

The host discovers assemblies under Mods beside the executable. It resolves dependencies, registers component types, calls mod entry points, and starts the registered systems. Simulation ticks update systems and then deliver gameplay events. Input events also run between tick batches so controls remain usable while paused.

docs.title: Reading order
docs.text:
1. Build a mod explains project setup, entry points, registration, deployment, and a complete behavior recipe.
  2. Loading and lifecycle explains discovery, dependencies, callback ordering, and cleanup.
  3. Entities and components covers every entity and command buffer call.
  4. Systems and queries covers system callbacks and query composition.
  5. Services and events covers communication between mods.
  6. Time and input covers every clock property, control request, and input event.
  7. Troubleshooting explains common failures and verification.

docs.title: Context properties
docs.text: IModContext lives in CitizenSimulator.Abstractions.Modding. Its properties expose shared objects rather than separate worlds for each mod.

docs.title: Services
docs.text: IServiceRegistry shares typed service objects. Register your public interface during OnLoad, then retrieve a dependency through its registered interface type.

docs.title: Store
docs.text: IEntityStore reads entities and components. Direct structural changes are available before systems start. During callbacks, use the supplied command buffer for creation, destruction, attachment, and removal.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: IComponentRegistry registers component types and returns query tokens. Component registration describes a type. Attaching a component creates data on an entity. These are separate operations.

docs.title: Systems
docs.text: ISystemRegistry collects GameSystem instances. Register systems during OnLoad so the scheduler includes them in its startup snapshot.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: IEventBus queues gameplay events for delivery after system updates. Events published by a gameplay event handler wait for the next gameplay dispatch.

docs.title: InputEvents
docs.text: A separate IEventBus delivers input even when the simulation is paused. Subscribe here for keyboard events, submitted console lines, and control failures.

docs.title: Clock
docs.text: ISimulationClock exposes simulation state for inspection. Use the SimulationTime supplied to a callback for the destination time of the tick currently executing.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: ISimulationControls queues requests that the host applies between ticks. A request does not immediately change the clock.

docs.title: Using this guide
docs.text:
Start with the tutorial to create your own component, system, and event. Use the reference pages when implementing loading, world changes, communication, or input.

Call sequences are pseudocode. Translate them into valid C# when implementing your mod. XML project examples are usable as written.

docs.title: IServiceRegistry
docs.text: The service registry is a shared map keyed by the exact generic type used for registration. It does not construct dependencies or search assignable types.

docs.title:
Register(T service)

Stores a nonnull service object under typeof(T). T must be a reference type. Registering that type twice throws. To expose a public contract, explicitly choose the interface as T.

context.Services.Register<IGreetingService>(new GreetingService())

Registering only GreetingService does not make Get<IGreetingService>() work automatically.

Get()

Returns the object registered under that exact type. Throws InvalidOperationException when absent. Use for required dependencies after declaring their provider's mod ID in Dependencies.

greeting = context.Services.Get<IGreetingService>()

TryGet(out T? service)

Returns true and the service when registered. Returns false and null when absent. Use for optional integrations, while remembering that an independent provider might load later if no dependency orders the mods.

The registry offers no replacement, removal, or automatic disposal operation. Let a system own resources that need cleanup and dispose them in OnStop.
Event contracts
docs.text:
IEvent is an empty marker interface. Define a class or record implementing it for each public event contract. Prefer immutable payloads or captured values when listeners should observe the state at publication time.

Passing a mutable component in an event payload passes the same object reference. Later mutations can change what listeners observe before delivery.

EventHandler<TEvent> is a delegate with parameters TEvent eventData, SimulationTime time, and ICommandBuffer commandBuffer. TEvent must implement IEvent. The handler returns void. Its buffer follows the same lifetime and structural mutation rules as a system callback.

docs.title:
Publish(TEvent eventData)

Queues a nonnull payload under the exact generic event type. It does not synchronously invoke listeners. Publishing as IEvent addresses subscribers for IEvent, rather than subscribers for the concrete runtime type. Use the same concrete event type at publication and subscription.

Subscribe(EventHandler handler)

Registers a nonnull handler for that exact event type and returns an IDisposable subscription. Keep the returned object and call Dispose() to unsubscribe. Repeated disposal is harmless. Duplicate subscriptions are separate registrations and can cause repeated delivery.

Each subscriber receives a separate command buffer. A successful subscriber's structural changes play before the next subscriber runs.
Delivery order
docs.text:
Gameplay publication uses context.Events. After all system updates, dispatch snapshots and clears pending events. Events in that snapshot run in publication order. For each event, listeners are snapshotted in subscription order.

An event published by a handler is queued for the next dispatch. Gameplay dispatch normally occurs once per simulation tick, so handler generated gameplay events wait until the next tick. A paused simulation does not automatically deliver gameplay events.

A disposed subscription in an existing listener snapshot skips invocation. A new listener added during delivery does not join the current event's snapshot, though it can receive a later event in that dispatch.

An unhandled listener exception faults scheduled delivery. There is no automatic retry or transaction rollback.

docs.title: Choosing communication
docs.text:
Use a service when the caller needs an immediate result, for example checking stock or attempting a transfer. Use an event when announcing something to interested listeners, for example that a citizen was created. Use InputEvents for user actions that must work without an advancing simulation.

Regular entity store and event bus operations are not concurrent APIs. Keep mod world operations on scheduled callbacks. The host's input dispatcher and control request queue supply their own synchronization for their specific purposes.

docs.title: EntityRef
docs.text:
EntityRef(int Id, int Generation, int StoreId) is a value identifying an entity within a store. Equality includes all three fields. Do not construct references from a guessed ID. The current implementation issues increasing IDs with generation 1 and assigns each store its own identifier.

The default value is a detached or absent reference. A reserved entity returned by a command buffer is also not alive until its create command plays. Use Store.IsAlive(entity) before reading a reference that might have been destroyed.

docs.title: Component contracts
docs.text:
IComponent exposes Parent. Its setter is internal to the contract. Component<T> implements this contract and gives derived components a publicly readable parent. Prefer deriving from Component<YourComponent> rather than implementing parent bookkeeping yourself.

The engine assigns Parent during direct attachment or when attachment is queued. A queued parent therefore does not prove that the component is already in the store. Removal, entity destruction, or discarded unattached commands clear the parent to its default value.

A component instance cannot belong to different entities simultaneously. Use a fresh instance for each entity. Components are stored by the exact generic type supplied to AddComponent<T>, so use the concrete component type consistently.

docs.title: CreateEntity()
docs.text: Returns a new active EntityRef immediately. Use during mod loading or other host controlled setup outside scheduled callbacks. During callbacks call commands.CreateEntity() instead.

docs.title: DestroyEntity(EntityRef entity)
docs.text: Immediately removes a live entity and clears all attached component parents. Invalid or destroyed references throw. Use the command buffer during callbacks.

docs.title: IsAlive(EntityRef entity)
docs.text: Returns whether the reference belongs to this store, has the expected generation, and currently identifies an active entity. Returns false for pending reservations, destroyed references, and foreign references.

docs.title:
AddComponent(EntityRef entity, T component)

Immediately attaches and returns the same component instance. T must be a class implementing IComponent. The entity must be alive, the instance must be nonnull, and the entity must not already contain this exact component type. Attaching a duplicate throws rather than replacing data. During callbacks use the command buffer.

GetComponent(EntityRef entity)

Returns the component or null when that type is absent on a live entity. An invalid entity throws rather than returning null. Reading returns the stored reference, so changing its properties changes shared state immediately.

HasComponent(EntityRef entity)

Reports whether a live entity contains the exact component type. An invalid entity throws. This call cannot see attachments waiting in a command buffer.

RemoveComponent(EntityRef entity)

Immediately removes the type when present and clears the detached component's parent. Missing components are harmless on a valid entity. Invalid entities throw. Use the command buffer during callbacks.

Query(IQuery query)

Lazily enumerates active entities whose component dictionaries match the query. A null query throws. Avoid direct structural mutation while enumerating. Queue structural work for the end of the callback instead.
ICommandBuffer calls
docs.text: Every method operates on the current callback's buffer. Never retain the buffer for another callback, another thread, or later asynchronous work. Playback and discard close it permanently.

docs.title:
CreateEntity()

Reserves and returns an EntityRef, then queues activation. You may queue component attachments to this reference in the same buffer. Store reads still reject it until playback activates it.

DestroyEntity(EntityRef entity)

Queues strict destruction. The reference must belong to this store and must not be reserved by another buffer. Liveness is enforced when the command executes. Destroying an already destroyed entity causes playback failure.

TryDestroyEntity(EntityRef entity)

Queues destruction only if the entity is alive when playback reaches the command. Useful when multiple operations might destroy the same entity. Foreign references and reservations owned by another buffer still throw when queued. This is not a universal validation bypass.

AddComponent(EntityRef entity, T component)

Queues attachment and immediately returns the supplied object. Parent is assigned when queued, so you can configure the returned component before attachment. Duplicate type checks happen during playback. Repeated additions of the same type can therefore fail after earlier commands have already succeeded.

RemoveComponent(EntityRef entity)

Queues removal. Missing types are harmless at playback if the entity is alive. Removing from an entity destroyed by an earlier command fails validation.
Creating related state
docs.text:
This is pseudocode for a callback that creates an entity and attaches data.

entity = commands.CreateEntity()
counter = commands.AddComponent(entity, new CounterComponent { Count = 0 })
counter.Count = 5

Do not call Store.GetComponent<CounterComponent>(entity) in this sequence. The reference is still reserved. Retain the returned component object for work within this callback and read through the store in later callbacks.

docs.title: Component registry calls
docs.text:
IComponentRegistry.Register<T>() registers the type and returns ComponentType<T>. Registering the same type again returns its existing token.

IComponentRegistry.Get<T>() returns an existing token and throws when the type is unregistered. IComponentRegistry.IsRegistered<T>() checks registration without throwing for absence.

ComponentTypes.Initialize(IComponentRegistry registry) sets the global registry used by static helpers. The host calls it before loading mods. Mods should use the supplied registry rather than reinitialize this shared state.

ComponentTypes.Get<T>() forwards to that registry and throws if initialization has not occurred or the type is absent. Component<T>.GetComponentType() is the convenient inherited form.

ComponentType<T>(int Id) implements IQuery. Its Matches method checks the presence of typeof(T) in a component dictionary. The numeric ID is registry metadata rather than a persistent identifier to save or transmit.

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
The host creates Mods under AppContext.BaseDirectory when necessary. ModLoader recursively examines DLL files there and loads them into the default assembly load context. It considers concrete classes implementing IMod that have a ModAttribute.

The loader uses Activator.CreateInstance, so entry points need an accessible constructor without arguments. Assembly and construction errors are logged during discovery. IDs must contain text. ID comparisons are case insensitive. When multiple discovered mods share an ID, the entire conflicting group is excluded.

The assembly resolver maps simple assembly names to DLL paths under Mods. Avoid multiple DLLs with the same assembly name because the path map can select only one. There is no isolated load context per mod and no automatic reload facility.

docs.title: ModAttribute
docs.text:
ModAttribute(string id, string name, string version) supplies identity and display metadata. Id, Name, and Version are readable properties. Dependencies is a writable string array containing required mod IDs. The attribute applies to classes and cannot be repeated on the same class.

Dependencies initialize before dependents. Missing dependencies and dependency cycles exclude affected mods from the valid load order. If a dependency throws during OnLoad, its dependents are skipped. Unrelated valid mods may still initialize.

The loader registers concrete closed component classes from valid mod assemblies before calling any OnLoad. It then calls entry points in dependency order. For otherwise independent mods, traversal begins in sorted ID order. Express ordering requirements with dependencies rather than depending on incidental file names.

Initialization is not transactional. A failed OnLoad can leave services, systems, entities, subscriptions, or queued events already registered. No automatic rollback or IMod unload callback exists.

docs.title: Scheduler lifetime
docs.text:
1. The scheduler snapshots Systems.GetSystems() during startup.
  2. Systems start in ascending priority order. Equal priorities retain registration order.
  3. Each successful tick calls every system's OnUpdate in that order.
  4. After system updates, the gameplay bus dispatches the events pending at the start of dispatch.
  5. Shutdown calls OnStop in reverse successful startup order.

Register all systems before scheduler startup. Registering one later changes the registry but does not update the scheduler's captured list.

Each start, update, stop, and event handler invocation receives a fresh command buffer. The world rejects direct structural changes during the invocation. After a successful invocation, queued commands play in submission order before the next invocation begins.

Commands do not wait until the next tick. For example, a component queued by the first system's OnStart is available to the second system's OnStart.

docs.title: Failures and cleanup
docs.text:
If a callback throws, its queued structural commands are discarded. Direct field mutations, service side effects, and published events are not rolled back. If command playback fails, commands already applied remain applied. Commands after the failure do not run.

A failed system startup triggers a cleanup attempt for that system followed by shutdown of already started systems. An update or event delivery failure faults the scheduler. The host reports the exception and attempts shutdown. A failed tick also faults the clock because world state cannot safely be rolled back.

Use OnStop to dispose subscriptions and release mod resources. Cleanup should tolerate partial initialization. The Store property remains assigned during OnStop and is cleared afterward even if cleanup throws.

docs.title: GameSystem
docs.text:
GameSystem(int priority = 0) is the base class for scheduled behavior. Smaller priorities run first. The Priority property is readable and fixed at construction. Name is virtual and defaults to the concrete class name.

Store is a protected IEntityStore. The scheduler assigns it before OnStart and clears it after OnStop. Avoid accessing it from the system constructor.

docs.title: OnStart(ICommandBuffer commands)
docs.text: Override this protected virtual callback to cache queries, subscribe to events, and queue initial entities or attachments. The default implementation does nothing. Structural commands play before the next system starts.

docs.title: OnUpdate(SimulationTime time, ICommandBuffer commands)
docs.text: Override this protected virtual callback for tick behavior. Read matching entities through Store, mutate existing data directly when appropriate, and queue structural changes. time describes the destination simulation time for this tick.

docs.title: OnStop(ICommandBuffer commands)
docs.text: Override this protected virtual callback to dispose subscriptions and release resources. Cleanup callbacks also receive a command buffer. Gameplay events published during shutdown are not automatically followed by another gameplay dispatch.

docs.title: Public lifecycle wrappers
docs.text:
Start(IEntityStore store, ICommandBuffer commands) validates arguments, assigns Store, and calls OnStart.

Update(SimulationTime time, ICommandBuffer commands) validates the buffer and calls OnUpdate.

Stop(ICommandBuffer commands) validates the buffer, invokes OnStop, and clears Store in a finally block.

These wrappers exist for the host scheduler. A mod normally overrides the protected callbacks and lets the scheduler invoke them. Calling wrappers yourself bypasses normal scheduler lifetime management.

docs.title: ISystemRegistry
docs.text:
Register(GameSystem system) adds a nonnull instance. Registering another instance of the same concrete runtime type throws. Different concrete system types may share a displayed name.

IsRegistered<T>() reports whether the exact system type is registered. GetSystems() returns a priority sorted list. Equal priorities preserve registration order. The engine caches this list and invalidates its cache when registration succeeds.

The scheduler takes a separate snapshot during startup, so registry changes afterward do not add running systems.

docs.title: Query calls
docs.text:
IQuery.Matches(IReadOnlyDictionary<Type, IComponent> components) evaluates an entity's component set. Implement this interface for a custom predicate when composition is insufficient. The supplied dictionary contains live component references.

Query.And(params IQuery[] queries) creates an AndQuery requiring every child to match. An empty list matches every entity.

Query.Or(params IQuery[] queries) creates an OrQuery requiring any child to match. An empty list matches no entities.

Query.Not(IQuery query) creates a NotQuery that inverts its child.

You can also construct AndQuery, OrQuery, and NotQuery directly with the same arguments. And and Or copy the supplied array. Null arrays, null children, and a null Not child are rejected.

docs.title: Query composition example
docs.text:
Define your own CounterComponent, EnabledComponent, and CompletedComponent types. To process enabled counters that have not completed, cache this expression during OnStart after registering all three types.

Query.And(
    CounterComponent.GetComponentType(),
    EnabledComponent.GetComponentType(),
    Query.Not(CompletedComponent.GetComponentType())
)

To match either of your own marker types, such as PendingComponent and ActiveComponent, use this expression. Register both types before constructing the query.

Query.Or(
    PendingComponent.GetComponentType(),
    ActiveComponent.GetComponentType()
)

Component queries test presence rather than property values. After retrieving a component, inspect its fields for conditions such as Count or a completion flag. Alternatively, implement a custom IQuery that reads those properties.

docs.title: SimulationTime
docs.text:
SimulationTime(ulong Tick, TimeSpan Delta, TimeSpan Elapsed) is the callback time value. Tick is the destination tick number. Delta is the fixed simulation duration of one tick. Elapsed is the simulation timestamp at that destination.

Inside a tick callback the shared clock can still report the previously completed tick. The clock commits the destination tick after all work for the tick succeeds. Use the callback argument when calculating current tick behavior.

docs.title: ISimulationClock properties
docs.text:
TickRate is the configured number of simulation ticks per simulation second. The host defaults to 30.

Tick is the latest committed tick, initially zero. Delta is the fixed tick duration. Elapsed is total simulation time at the committed tick, rather than wall clock time.

IsPaused reports whether normal time accumulation is paused. Speed is the positive real time multiplier, initially 1. Speed changes the pace of ticks while leaving each tick's simulation duration fixed.

IsAdvancing reports an active manual target. It can be true while IsPaused is also true because manual advancement executes ticks without resuming normal time accumulation.

The host defaults to batches of at most 8 ticks, allowing input and queued controls to be processed between batches. Controls are also applied after each completed tick.

docs.title: ISimulationControls calls
docs.text: Requests are queued and applied in submission order between ticks. Reading the clock immediately after requesting a change may show the old state. The host handles up to 64 queued requests per application pass.

docs.title: Pause()
docs.text: Pauses normal advancement and cancels an active manual target. Use this to establish the state required for stepping or to cancel a long advance.

docs.title: Resume()
docs.text: Resumes normal accumulation. Fails if a manual target is still active. Queue Pause() before Resume() when cancelling an advance and returning to normal running.

docs.title: SetSpeed(double speed)
docs.text: Sets the real time multiplier. The value must be finite and greater than zero. Zero is invalid, so use Pause() to stop advancement.

docs.title: Step(ulong count = 1)
docs.text: Runs the requested positive number of ticks while remaining paused afterward. Requires a paused clock with no active manual target. A count of zero is invalid. The target is calculated from the current committed tick when the queued request is applied.

docs.title: AdvanceBy(TimeSpan duration)
docs.text: Advances relative to the current simulation elapsed time. Requires a paused clock without an active target. Duration must be nonnegative. A duration of zero completes without scheduling extra ticks.

docs.title: AdvanceTo(TimeSpan target)
docs.text: Advances to an absolute simulation timestamp. Requires a paused clock without an active target. The target cannot precede the current elapsed time. A target between tick boundaries rounds upward to the first tick reaching that timestamp. The exposed current timestamp is recognized without adding a tick.

docs.title: Quit()
docs.text:
Requests host cancellation. The host exits its main loop and stops systems. This uses the normal shutdown path.

Invalid queued control arguments, invalid state, and arithmetic overflow are reported as ControlFailed events on InputEvents. Subscribe to these events to display errors. Validation happens when the request is applied, so a try block around the request alone does not receive those failures.

docs.title: Input event types
docs.text:
All input events are in CitizenSimulator.Abstractions.Input and implement IEvent.

KeyPressed(InputKey Key, KeyModifiers Modifiers) reports a transition to held state. Repeated native presses while already held do not produce another transition event.

KeyReleased(InputKey Key, KeyModifiers Modifiers) reports a transition out of held state.

KeyHeld(InputKey Key, KeyModifiers Modifiers) is published once per simulation tick for each held key. It does not continue firing while fully paused. Its modifier value comes from the dispatcher's latest modifier state.

LineSubmitted(string Text) reports a complete console line. ControlFailed(string Message) reports a rejected queued control operation.

Pressed, released, and submitted line events are drained between batches even while paused. Between batch input callbacks receive a time value with zero Delta and the current committed time. Held callbacks run before system updates with the destination tick time.

docs.title: Key values
docs.text:
InputKey includes Unknown, Enter, Escape, Space, Left, Right, Up, Down, Backspace, Tab, Shift, Control, Alt, letters A through Z, and F1 through F12.

KeyModifiers is a flags enum. None is 0, Shift is 1, Control is 2, and Alt is 4. Combine flags when matching chords.

docs.title: IInputState.IsDown(InputKey key)
docs.text:
Retrieve IInputState through context.Services.Get<IInputState>(). The host registers it before loading mods. IsDown reports whether the dispatcher currently considers the key held. Unknown is not added to held state.

Native keyboard input is available through the Windows console adapter when it can be created. Otherwise the host falls back to submitted console lines, so keyboard transition events should not be assumed available on every host.

docs.title: Pause binding recipe
docs.text:
During a system's OnStart, subscribe to KeyPressed on context.InputEvents and keep the returned subscription. The handler can use this pseudocode.

if data.Key == InputKey.Space
    if context.Clock.IsPaused
        context.Controls.Resume()
    else
        context.Controls.Pause()

For a manual advance, enqueue calls in this order.

context.Controls.Pause()
context.Controls.AdvanceBy(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10))

Dispose the binding subscription during OnStop. Subscribe to ControlFailed to report errors if a request conflicts with another queued control.

docs.title: Add text controls
docs.text:
To add console commands to your mod, subscribe to LineSubmitted on context.InputEvents. Compare data.Text with command names you define, then queue the matching control request.

For example, handle pause with context.Controls.Pause() and resume with context.Controls.Resume(). Validate numeric arguments before requesting a speed change or a manual advance. Subscribe to ControlFailed to report requests rejected by the host.

Keep the subscription in a system and dispose it during OnStop.

docs.title: The mod never appears
docs.text: Confirm that its DLL is below Mods beside the executable being run. A folder named Mods at the repository root is not automatically searched. Check for a concrete IMod implementation, a ModAttribute, and a public constructor without arguments. Read discovery errors for missing assemblies or incompatible binaries.

docs.title: Duplicate ID or missing dependency
docs.text: IDs are case insensitive. All entries in a duplicate ID group are excluded. Dependencies contain mod IDs rather than project names or assembly names. Install each required provider DLL and remove cycles from dependency declarations.

docs.title: A service is not registered
docs.text: Check the exact generic registration type. A concrete class registration does not satisfy an interface lookup. Required providers must initialize first through a declared dependency. Ensure the providing entry point actually registers the interface during OnLoad.

docs.title: A system does not execute
docs.text: Register an instance through context.Systems.Register during OnLoad. Component discovery does not register systems. Registration after scheduler startup does not affect the captured system list. A fully paused simulation does not call OnUpdate until stepped, advanced, or resumed.

docs.title: Structural mutation throws
docs.text: Entity creation, destruction, component attachment, and removal must use the callback's command buffer during system and event callbacks. A service can also trigger this error if its implementation directly changes structure. Inspect your service implementation for direct store calls and pass the callback buffer when queueing structural changes.

docs.title: A new entity is invalid
docs.text:
A reference returned by commands.CreateEntity() is reserved until playback. Attach data through the same buffer and use the returned component object within the callback. Read it through the store only after the callback succeeds and playback completes.

Services that call Store.HasComponent before queueing an attachment also require an already live entity. Their signatures accepting a command buffer do not imply support for a pending entity.

docs.title: An event seems delayed or missing
docs.text: Check the bus and generic event type. Gameplay events dispatch after systems and wait while paused. Events published by gameplay handlers wait for another dispatch. Input subscriptions belong on InputEvents. Keep subscriptions alive and dispose them only at the end of their intended lifetime.

docs.title: A control request has no immediate effect
docs.text: Controls are applied later in submission order. Inspect subsequent clock state or listen for ControlFailed. Pause before stepping or advancing. Pause again to cancel an active target before requesting another manual advance or resuming.

docs.title: Partial changes remain after failure
docs.text: Command playback is ordered without rollback. Earlier commands can succeed before a later command fails. Direct data changes and service effects are also not rolled back when a callback throws. Validate inputs before mutation and avoid duplicate queued attachments.

docs.title: Verification recipe
docs.text:
1. Build the host and mod against the same abstraction assembly.
  2. Install the mod and all required providers under the executable's Mods directory.
  3. Confirm successful load messages for every dependency and the mod itself.
  4. Check one startup operation and one update operation with observable output.
  5. Confirm that a command from an earlier system is visible to a later system in the same tick.
  6. Pause and verify that submitted input still reaches its listener.
  7. Step once and confirm that the simulation performs exactly one update per registered system.
  8. Quit and confirm subscription cleanup and system shutdown.

docs.title: Create the project
docs.text:
Use the .NET 10 SDK. Create a class library beside the existing projects, for example ExampleMod/ExampleMod.csproj. Reference the same abstraction project that the host uses.

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <ProjectReference Include="../CitizenSimulator.Abstractions/CitizenSimulator.Abstractions.csproj" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>

Reference a shared contract assembly when your mod uses types defined outside the core abstractions. Declare the providing mod ID when it must initialize first. A project reference makes types available to the compiler. A mod dependency controls runtime initialization order.

docs.title: Define the entry point
docs.text:
Create a public concrete class called ExampleMod implementing CitizenSimulator.Abstractions.Modding.IMod. Give it a public constructor with no arguments, or use the implicit constructor. Apply this attribute to the class.

[Mod("example", "Example mod", "1.0.0")]

Implement void OnLoad(IModContext context). The loader calls it once for this load attempt after required dependencies have initialized. Keep constructors free of world setup because discovery constructs mod instances before initialization order has been resolved.

If you create a separate mod that provides a shared service, declare its ID as a dependency. For a provider you name example_services, metadata looks like this.

[Mod("example", "Example mod", "1.0.0", Dependencies = new[] { "example_services" })]

The displayed version is descriptive metadata. The loader does not enforce version ranges.

docs.title: Define component data
docs.text:
Create a public class CounterComponent deriving from Component<CounterComponent>. Add an integer property called Count with public accessors. The base class supplies Parent and GetComponentType().

Component types in valid discovered mod assemblies are registered automatically before any mod receives OnLoad. For component classes in a separate helper assembly without a discovered mod entry point, explicitly register the type through context.Components.Register<CounterComponent>().

docs.title: Register behavior
docs.text:
Create a public class CounterSystem deriving from GameSystem. Its constructor accepts an IEventBus and stores it for later publication. Give the base constructor priority 10 if this system should run after systems with priority 0.

Inside OnLoad, perform this pseudocode sequence.

context.Systems.Register(new CounterSystem(context.Events))
entity = context.Store.CreateEntity()
context.Store.AddComponent(entity, new CounterComponent { Count = 0 })

The entity and component are immediately visible because loading happens before scheduled execution. Systems are registered explicitly. Discovering a mod does not automatically register its systems.

docs.title: Implement callbacks
docs.text:
Override OnStart(ICommandBuffer commands) and cache the component query.

counterQuery = CounterComponent.GetComponentType()

Override OnUpdate(SimulationTime time, ICommandBuffer commands) with this pseudocode.

for each entity in Store.Query(counterQuery)
    counter = Store.GetComponent<CounterComponent>(entity)
    if counter is null
        continue
    counter.Count = counter.Count + 1
    if counter.Count >= 30
        events.Publish(new CounterCompleted(entity, counter.Count))
        commands.RemoveComponent<CounterComponent>(entity)

Define CounterCompleted as an immutable class or record implementing IEvent, with EntityRef Entity and int Count data. The example counts updates, so the real elapsed duration depends on the configured tick rate. Use time.Delta.TotalSeconds for behavior expressed in simulation seconds.

Removing the component takes effect when this callback finishes successfully. A later system in the same tick can see the removal. The completion event is delivered after all system updates finish.

docs.title: Receive the completion event
docs.text:
Create a listener system whose OnStart stores the subscription returned by this call.

events.Subscribe<CounterCompleted>(HandleCompleted)

The handler signature is void HandleCompleted(CounterCompleted data, SimulationTime time, ICommandBuffer commands). It can inspect data.Entity, print data.Count, or queue further changes. Check Store.IsAlive(data.Entity) before accessing entity data because references can become stale before event delivery.

Override OnStop and call Dispose() on the stored subscription. Register the listener system during OnLoad. This gives the subscription a clear lifetime and prevents abandoned listeners.

docs.title: Build and install
docs.text:
Run these commands from the repository root after creating the project.

dotnet build ExampleMod/ExampleMod.csproj
dotnet build CitizenSimulator/CitizenSimulator.csproj

Copy ExampleMod/bin/Debug/net10.0/ExampleMod.dll into CitizenSimulator/bin/Debug/net10.0/Mods/ExampleMod/. Copy any additional required mod and helper assemblies into the Mods tree as well. Use the abstraction assembly supplied by the host and avoid distributing competing copies of shared assemblies.

Start the host with these commands from the repository root.

cd CitizenSimulator
